title: Cross Laminated Timber Joint Explorer
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements an interactive Cross Laminated Timber (CLT) joint explorer for architectural education. Load the 'Xbot.glb' model using GLTFLoader from the Three.js examples CDN and place it in the scene as a reference human-scale figure for size comparison.

## Scene Setup
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 3, 8) looking at the origin.
- Add OrbitControls for camera manipulation.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light at (5, 10, 5) with intensity 0.8 and shadow mapping enabled.
- Set the background to a light gray gradient (0xd0d0d0).
- Add a ground plane grid helper (20x20) for spatial reference.

## CLT Panel System
- Create a CLT panel assembly consisting of TWO rectangular timber panels that form a joint.
- Panel A (horizontal base): 4m x 0.2m x 2m box geometry, wood-colored material (0xC19A6B) with slight roughness.
- Panel B (vertical wall): 0.2m x 3m x 2m box geometry, slightly different wood tone (0xD2A679).
- Panel B sits on top of Panel A, forming an L-shaped joint at the origin.
- Each panel should have visible layer lines: add 5 thin stripe meshes on each panel face to represent the alternating grain direction layers of CLT (odd layers horizontal grain, even layers at 90 degrees). Use slightly darker color (0xA0784B) for these stripes.

## Joint Types (4 types, switchable)
- Implement 4 joint configurations the user can cycle through:
  1. 'butt' - Panel B simply sits on Panel A with no interlock (default).
  2. 'half_lap' - Panel B drops 0.1m into Panel A (Panel A gets a notch cutout represented by moving Panel B down 0.1 and adding a notch indicator mesh).
  3. 'dovetail' - Panel B base widens with a trapezoidal connector mesh (add a tapered box between panels, wider at bottom).
  4. 'steel_bracket' - Add two visible L-shaped steel bracket meshes (metallic gray 0x888888, metalness 0.8) on either side of the joint.
- Pressing keys 1-4 switches joint type. Animate the transition over 500ms.

## Exploded View
- Pressing 'E' toggles exploded view: panels separate apart (Panel A moves down 1m, Panel B moves up 1m, any connector elements spread proportionally) with a smooth 600ms animation.
- Pressing 'E' again collapses back to assembled position.

## Layer Visibility
- Pressing 'L' cycles through layer visibility modes: 'all' (default), 'odd_only' (show only odd-numbered CLT layers), 'even_only' (show only even-numbered layers). This helps visualize the cross-lamination pattern.

## Load Analysis Overlay
- Pressing 'F' toggles a force/load analysis overlay:
  - When active, show colored arrow helpers indicating load paths: a downward red arrow on Panel B (gravity load), reaction arrows (green) at the joint, and a blue arrow showing lateral resistance.
  - Display a HUD text showing estimated joint strength as a percentage (butt=40%, half_lap=65%, dovetail=80%, steel_bracket=95%).

## Measurement Tool
- Pressing 'M' toggles measurement mode. When active, display dimension lines (using Line geometry) showing Panel A width, Panel B height, and joint overlap depth. Show measurement values as HTML overlay labels positioned via CSS2DRenderer or absolute-positioned divs updated each frame.

## Xbot Reference Figure
- Load 'Xbot.glb' and place it at position (3, 0, 0) scaled so it stands approximately 1.8m tall. This provides human-scale reference.
- The model should be visible and cast shadows.

## HUD / UI
- Top-left HUD panel (HTML overlay, semi-transparent dark background) showing:
  - Current joint type name
  - Exploded view status (on/off)
  - Layer visibility mode
  - Force overlay status (on/off)
  - Measurement mode status (on/off)
  - Joint strength percentage
- Bottom bar with 4 buttons labeled 'Butt Joint', 'Half-Lap', 'Dovetail', 'Steel Bracket' that also switch joint types (same as keys 1-4).

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
  - jointType: string ('butt'|'half_lap'|'dovetail'|'steel_bracket')
  - exploded: boolean
  - layerMode: string ('all'|'odd_only'|'even_only')
  - forceOverlay: boolean
  - measurementMode: boolean
  - jointStrength: number (percentage 0-100)
  - panelAPositionY: number (Panel A world Y position)
  - panelBPositionY: number (Panel B world Y position)
  - separationDistance: number (distance between panel centers)
  - bracketCount: number (number of visible bracket meshes, 0 or 2)
  - visibleLayers: number (count of currently visible layer stripe meshes)
  - totalLayers: number (total layer stripe meshes)
  - arrowCount: number (number of visible force arrows)
  - xbotLoaded: boolean
  - xbotPositionX: number
  - cameraDistance: number (distance from camera to origin)
  - animating: boolean (true during any transition animation)
  - measurementLabelsVisible: boolean
physics_constraints: Joint strength values must be consistent with joint type (butt=40, half_lap=65, dovetail=80, steel_bracket=95). Exploded view separation must be symmetric. Panel positions must be NaN-free at all times. Layer count arithmetic must be consistent (visible layers + hidden layers = total layers). Force arrows should only appear when force overlay is active.
